M1.reason: Silhouette overlap is 0.952 (front/back), 0.964 (left/right) and 0.950 (top/below), all above 0.80. In the six side-by-side views the outlines match, with nothing sticking out or missing. The reproduction's head sits slightly further forward and its helmet is a little flatter in the left and right views, but the measured overlap covers that.

M2.reason: Size is 22.7 x 29.9 x 75.1 against the original's 22.8 x 30.2 x 75.3, off by 0.2 to 0.9%. That is well within 10% on every axis.

M3.reason: Every component is there in the right place and shape: the helmet with its visor, the black vest with its chest and shoulder straps, the yellow emblem on the chest, the 'SECURITY' panel on the back, the holster and pistol on the hip, the belt, the trousers and the laced boots. Counts match: two arms, two legs, two boots, one helmet.

M4.reason: The measured colour difference is 6.1 on average (CIE76 ΔE), with each view between 5.1 and 7.8, well under 15. Shirt and trousers are the same purple-blue, the vest and boots the same black, the emblem the same yellow. The face reads slightly greyer and more mottled, but that is texture, which M5 covers, not a change of colour.

M5.reason: The markings are present in their places but softer than the original's. The 'SECURITY' lettering on the back is blurred where the original is crisp, the vest's panel seams and the chest emblem are less defined, and the face has a smeared, noisy texture where the original has clean skin and features. The helmet glare is also flatter.

The face is mottled and blurred, the helmet looks duller and sits slightly differently, and the run in the motion strip has a different cadence (22 frames against the original's 15). It is clearly short of passing for the original on a close look.

M7.reason: The front faces forward, the figure stands upright, and its feet sit on the same ground line as the original's in every view, so it stands on its origin as the original does.

M8.reason: The SMAK check reports no errors. The reproduction has 362 triangles against the original's 785, so it is well under twice the original's count. No part is open, inside out or floating in any of the views.

C1.reason: Nothing comes apart, sinks or floats through the run in the motion strip, so the parts stay on the body. But the motion does not match the original's. The original leans forward with wide arm swings, while the reproduction's torso is more upright and its arms are held close in frames 3/22 and 6/22. Its stride and cadence differ too. The strip shows only the run, not an attack, so the attack is not judged.
